chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the man who performs the ritual bath (ghusl) in Medina for his Ihram. Does that suffice him from the Ghusl of Dhu al-Hulayfa? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Yes.' Then a man came to him while I was in his presence, and he said: 'One of our companions performed a ritual bath, and a need presented itself to him until evening.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should repeat the ritual bath. His bathing during the day is for that day of his, and at night is for his night.'

key_terms.يُجْزِئُهُ: Suffice him / be valid for him

ai.seo_question: Does performing Ghusl for Ihram in Medina suffice if done away from the Miqat, and what happens if one needs to urinate afterwards?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that performing Ghusl for Ihram in Medina suffices as the Miqat ritual bath, affirming the flexibility of the sacred boundary. It further provides a practical legal distinction: if a pilgrim's state of purity is broken by a need during the day, they must repeat the bath for that day, and similarly for the night, ensuring the ritual integrity of the Ihram state is maintained throughout the transition.
